key_results: W15 sample optimal shield at 662 keV; LAC values rise with density; experimental, GEANT4, MCNP, XCOM results agree within 5%; sample W15 LAC = (0.1047 ± 0.0014, 0.1045, 0.1018, 0.1047 cm⁻¹)
comments: Good agreement across experimental and computational methods; biocompatible material candidate for medical/nuclear applications, though limited to 662 keV energy.

outputs: MAC, LAC, HVL, TVL, MFP, Zeff, Neff, LET parameters

hypotheses.hypothesis: Increasing WO3 doping density improves photon shielding
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; LAC increases monotonically with density; W15 selected as optimal

title: Host-aware Identification of Intrinsic Gene Expression Biopart Parameters using Combinatorial Libraries
task: Host-aware characterization of biopart parameters in combinatorial expression libraries
key_results: Identified mechanistically interpretable, transferable parameters for plasmid origins, promoters, and RBS across physiological conditions
Defined intrinsic translation initiation capacity that predicts protein synthesis with improved accuracy across contexts
comments: The digital twin approach effectively decouples biopart properties from host physiology, but practical scalability to more complex multi-gene circuits remains to be demonstrated.

model_io.model: Digital twin of E. coli conditioned on growth rate with model-in-the-loop parameter identification
inputs: Combinatorial plasmid construct libraries (origins, promoters, RBS variants)
outputs: Intrinsic biopart parameters (promoter strength, RBS translation capacity)
Predicted protein synthesis rates across physiological conditions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Biopart-associated properties can be separated from host-dependent effects using host-aware parameterization
hypotheses.result: Successfully identified transferable parameters for origins, promoters, and RBS that predict expression across conditions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local sequence context modulates expression beyond intrinsic biopart properties
hypotheses.result: Revealed localized failures of modularity, indicating context-dependent expression emerges from host physiology and sequence context
